propositions: The reconciler writes the cursor unconditionally to the newest event timestamp after each pass, advancing past candidates it failed to vote, permanently excluding them from future windows via server-side ?t1= filtering.
A change with a timeout or error status on first-pass scan is never retried; it is silently forgotten despite documented contract that it should be re-driven.
Multiple patch-set uploads stall at zero votes while the reconciler votes on newer changes in the same window, proving the failure is per-upload not queue-wide.
The cursor must be a low-water mark clamped to the oldest retryably-abandoned candidate, so a failed candidate re-enters the next window until voted or the holdback timeout expires.

The three operational states (bot down, review running, queued vs dropped) are not observable; queue_depth and held_back metrics must be exposed so operators can distinguish stalled from normal backlog.
